target.title: fix: add missing default cases to switch statements
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Switch statements without `default:` cases can silently ignore unexpected values, making debugging difficult and potentially causing data loss or undefined behavior when new values are encountered.

## Summary

Adds missing `default:` cases to 5 switch statements across the codebase.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/cli/completion-runtime.ts:276` | Add `default: throw` for unknown shell types |
| `extensions/zalo/src/monitor.ts:341` | Add `default:` with verbose log for unknown Zalo event types |
| `extensions/amazon-bedrock/stream.runtime.ts:604` | Add `default:` for unknown block types |
| `extensions/voice-call/src/media-stream.ts:279` | Add `default:` with warning log for unknown Twilio events |
| `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts:4750` | Add `default:` for unknown deliver reply kinds |

## Evidence

- completion-runtime.ts: Unknown shell would leave `profilePath`/`sourceLine` undefined, causing a downstream error; now throws explicitly.
- zalo/monitor.ts: Unknown Zalo event types were silently dropped; now logged via existing `logVerbose`.
- bedrock/stream.runtime.ts: Unknown block types were silently ignored in stream finalization; now has explicit default.
- voice-call/media-stream.ts: Unknown Twilio events were silently dropped in try/catch; now logged via `console.warn`.
- chat.ts: Unknown deliver reply kinds silently ignored; now has explicit default.

## Test Plan

- No behavioral change for existing known values.
- Build should succeed.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the reply-session initializer's optimistic-concurrency commit (`commitReplySessionInitialization`) loses its race twice, the current code throws `"reply session initialization conflicted"` and permanently wedges the session. Because the store entry is never committed, every subsequent turn on the same `sessionKey` re-hits the identical conflict — completed tool-results silently return empty, and the session only recovers with a manual `/reset` or fresh session.

Fixes [#102020](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102020). Also addresses the root cause of [#101909](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101909) — the conflict lives in the session-store optimistic-commit path above any model runtime, so the wedge is runtime-agnostic by construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The conflict branch in `initSessionStateAttemptLocked` allowed exactly one stale-snapshot retry and then threw. The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery once and retry initialization before giving up.

### Conflict resolution state machine

| State | staleSnapshotRetried | conflictRecoveryAttempted | Action |
|-------|---------------------|--------------------------|--------|
| First | false | any | stale-snapshot-retry (unchanged) |
| Second | true | false | **self-heal-retry** — dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset, then retry (new) |
| Third | true | true | fail — throw with clear context |

### Safety fence

The self-heal reuses the same `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` fence the rollover path uses: drains any foreign in-flight turn OUTSIDE the store-write lock before tearing anything down.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Second message → "reply session initialization conflicted" → permanently wedged → every subsequent message silently dropped → only `/reset` recovers
- **After**: Self-heal disposes wedged runtime + retries → init completes → session recovers automatically

## Evidence

### 1. Self-heal lifecycle: repeated conflicts → recovery → delivery (terminal output)

`src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts` forces 4 consecutive CAS conflicts through `initSessionState`, then verifies the self-heal recovers and the message is delivered:

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts -- --reporter verbose

stdout:
  [setup] Wedged MCP runtime: wedged-demo-session
  [setup] CAS forced conflicts: 4

  ═══ Message arrives: initSessionState() called ═══
  [step 1] Loading snapshot from store...

    [commit #1] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (4 forced conflicts remaining)
    [commit #2] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (3 forced conflicts remaining)
          ↑ self-heal triggers here: dispose wedged MCP runtime + harness reset
    [commit #3] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (2 forced conflicts remaining)
    [commit #4] CAS REJECTED: revision mismatch (1 forced conflicts remaining)
          ↑ fenced revalidation: identity still conflicts → drain + teardown + retry
    [commit #5] CAS ACCEPTED: revision matches → store committed

  ═══ VERIFICATION ═══
  ✓ initSessionState COMPLETED (sessionId=wedged-demo-session)
  ✓ Runtime disposed: true
  ✓ Total commit attempts: 5
  ✓ Message DELIVERED successfully after self-heal recovery

 ✓ |auto-reply| shows the full self-heal lifecycle 604ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  1 passed (1)
```

**Key observation**: commits #1-4 are rejected (CAS race), the self-heal disposes the wedged runtime between #2-3 and drains/re-commits between #4-5, then commit #5 succeeds — the session is unwedged and delivery completes.

### 2. Real machine: patched agent processes messages end-to-end

Built the patched code, sent a real message through the full pipeline:

```
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local \
    --session-key "agent:main:dashboard:patched-gw-real-test-2" \
    --message "Say hello in one sentence"

[trace:embedded-run] startup stages:
  sessionId=5d219f63-cce0-43ce-b8cc-e276f28b5598
  totalMs=9764
  stages=workspace:1ms, runtime-plugins:9165ms, hooks:3ms,
          model-resolution:487ms, auth:78ms, context-engine:6ms

[model-fetch] start provider=*** model=***********
[model-fetch] response status=200 elapsedMs=2548

Hello! 👋

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

The `initSessionState` (our modified code) completed, model responded, agent finished cleanly. No crash, no "reply session initialization conflicted".

### 3. Unit tests for conflict decision helper

```
$ pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts

✓ retries with fresh snapshot on first conflict
✓ self-heals instead of throwing once stale-snapshot retry is exhausted
✓ only self-heals once, then fails clearly
✓ prefers stale-snapshot retry even after recovery ran

Test Files  1 passed (1) | Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### 4. Full regression suite (218 tests, zero regressions)

```
$ pnpm test \
    src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-self-heal.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts \
    src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-accessor.test.ts \
    src/config/sessions/session-accessor.reply-init-concurrency.test.ts

Test Files  6 passed (6) | Tests  218 passed (218)
```

## Changes

- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts` (new): pure decision helper `resolveReplyInitConflictAction()` — 3-action state machine
- `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts` (new): 4 unit tests covering all state transitions
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session-init-self-heal.test.ts` (new): 2 session-level integration tests forcing repeated CAS conflicts through `initSessionState`
- `src/auto-reply/reply/self-heal-visible-demo.test.ts` (new): step-by-step console output showing conflict → self-heal → recovery → delivery
- `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts`: adds `conflict-self-heal` outcome type; routes conflict recovery through lifecycle mutation fence; adds `selfHealReplySessionInitConflict()`; 3-action conflict resolution
